data.title: Doc Layout
data.tagline: Combine section navigation, article content, and an on-page outline
data.description: A documentation layout often uses a left navigation for pages, a readable center column for the article, and a right outline for headings. Keep each column's job distinct and collapse secondary navigation on small screens.

avoid: Give all three columns equal visual weight
Make the article column too wide to read
Show an outline that does not follow the headings
Keep side columns fixed on a narrow screen

lessonPractice.title: Technical docs need navigation across pages and within the current long article. Desktop has room but mobile is narrow. How should the layout adapt?

options.label: Use site navigation left, article center, and page outline right, progressively collapsing side columns on narrow screens
options.feedback: The columns handle cross-page access, reading, and in-page location separately, while collapse keeps content primary.

options.label: Keep three equal-width columns on every screen, including all directories on mobile
options.feedback: Navigation and outline do not deserve equal reading width, and three mobile columns make the article unusable.

options.label: Mix site pages and current headings into one long directory and use the rest for content
options.feedback: Mixing navigation scopes removes the boundary between opening another page and jumping within the current one.

data.agentPrompt: Implement a three-column docs layout: cross-page navigation left, constrained article center, and current-page anchors right. Hide the outline first on tablets and move site navigation into a mobile drawer. Verify page and section highlights stay distinct.
